scene.label: Act 4, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. A room in Petruchio's house.

lines.text: No, no, forsooth; I dare not for my life.
lines.plainText: No no forsooth I dare not for my life

lines.text: The more my wrong, the more his spite appears.
lines.plainText: The more my wrong the more his spite appears

lines.text: What, did he marry me to famish me?
lines.plainText: What did he marry me to famish me

lines.text: Beggars that come unto my father's door
lines.plainText: Beggars that come unto my father's door

lines.text: Upon entreaty have a present alms;
lines.plainText: Upon entreaty have a present alms

lines.text: If not, elsewhere they meet with charity;
lines.plainText: If not elsewhere they meet with charity

lines.text: But I, who never knew how to entreat,
lines.plainText: But I who never knew how to entreat

lines.text: Nor never needed that I should entreat,
lines.plainText: Nor never needed that I should entreat

lines.text: Am starv'd for meat, giddy for lack of sleep;
lines.plainText: Am starv'd for meat giddy for lack of sleep

lines.text: With oaths kept waking, and with brawling fed.
lines.plainText: With oaths kept waking and with brawling fed

lines.text: And that which spites me more than all these wants,
lines.plainText: And that which spites me more than all these wants

lines.text: He does it under name of perfect love;
lines.plainText: He does it under name of perfect love

lines.text: As who should say, if I should sleep or eat
lines.plainText: As who should say if I should sleep or eat

lines.text: 'Twere deadly sickness, or else present death.
lines.plainText: 'Twere deadly sickness or else present death

lines.text: I prithee go and get me some repast;
lines.plainText: I prithee go and get me some repast

lines.text: I care not what, so it be wholesome food.
lines.plainText: I care not what so it be wholesome food

lines.text: What say you to a neat's foot?
lines.plainText: What say you to a neat's foot

lines.text: 'Tis passing good; I prithee let me have it.
lines.plainText: 'Tis passing good I prithee let me have it

lines.text: I fear it is too choleric a meat.
lines.plainText: I fear it is too choleric a meat

lines.text: How say you to a fat tripe finely broil'd?
lines.plainText: How say you to a fat tripe finely broil'd

lines.text: I like it well; good Grumio, fetch it me.
lines.plainText: I like it well good Grumio fetch it me

lines.text: I cannot tell; I fear 'tis choleric.
lines.plainText: I cannot tell I fear 'tis choleric

lines.text: What say you to a piece of beef and mustard?
lines.plainText: What say you to a piece of beef and mustard

lines.text: A dish that I do love to feed upon.
lines.plainText: A dish that I do love to feed upon

lines.text: Ay, but the mustard is too hot a little.
lines.plainText: Ay but the mustard is too hot a little

lines.text: Why then the beef, and let the mustard rest.
lines.plainText: Why then the beef and let the mustard rest

lines.text: Nay, then I will not: you shall have the mustard,
lines.plainText: Nay then I will not you shall have the mustard

lines.text: Or else you get no beef of Grumio.
lines.plainText: Or else you get no beef of Grumio

lines.text: Then both, or one, or anything thou wilt.
lines.plainText: Then both or one or anything thou wilt

lines.text: Why then the mustard without the beef.
lines.plainText: Why then the mustard without the beef

lines.text: Go, get thee gone, thou false deluding slave,
lines.plainText: Go get thee gone thou false deluding slave

content.text: Enter Petruchio with a dish of meat; and Hortensio.

lines.text: How fares my Kate? What, sweeting, all amort?
lines.plainText: How fares my Kate What sweeting all amort

lines.text: Mistress, what cheer?
lines.plainText: Mistress what cheer

lines.text: Faith, as cold as can be.
lines.plainText: Faith as cold as can be

lines.text: Pluck up thy spirits; look cheerfully upon me.
lines.plainText: Pluck up thy spirits look cheerfully upon me

lines.text: Here, love; thou seest how diligent I am,
lines.plainText: Here love thou seest how diligent I am

lines.text: To dress thy meat myself, and bring it thee:
lines.plainText: To dress thy meat myself and bring it thee

lines.text: I pray you, let it stand.
lines.plainText: I pray you let it stand

lines.text: The poorest service is repaid with thanks;
lines.plainText: The poorest service is repaid with thanks

lines.text: And so shall mine, before you touch the meat.
lines.plainText: And so shall mine before you touch the meat

lines.text: I thank you, sir.
lines.plainText: I thank you sir

lines.text: Signior Petruchio, fie! you are to blame.
lines.plainText: Signior Petruchio fie you are to blame

lines.text: Come, Mistress Kate, I'll bear you company.
lines.plainText: Come Mistress Kate I'll bear you company

lines.text: [Aside.] Eat it up all, Hortensio, if thou lovest me.
lines.plainText: Aside Eat it up all Hortensio if thou lovest me

lines.text: Much good do it unto thy gentle heart!
lines.plainText: Much good do it unto thy gentle heart

lines.text: Kate, eat apace: and now, my honey love,
lines.plainText: Kate eat apace and now my honey love

lines.text: Will we return unto thy father's house
lines.plainText: Will we return unto thy father's house

lines.text: And revel it as bravely as the best,
lines.plainText: And revel it as bravely as the best

lines.text: With silken coats and caps, and golden rings,
lines.plainText: With silken coats and caps and golden rings

lines.text: With ruffs and cuffs and farthingales and things;
lines.plainText: With ruffs and cuffs and farthingales and things

lines.text: With scarfs and fans and double change of bravery,
lines.plainText: With scarfs and fans and double change of bravery

lines.text: With amber bracelets, beads, and all this knavery.
lines.plainText: With amber bracelets beads and all this knavery

lines.text: What! hast thou din'd? The tailor stays thy leisure,
lines.plainText: What hast thou din'd The tailor stays thy leisure

lines.text: To deck thy body with his ruffling treasure.
lines.plainText: To deck thy body with his ruffling treasure

lines.text: Here is the cap your worship did bespeak.
lines.plainText: Here is the cap your worship did bespeak

lines.text: Why, this was moulded on a porringer;
lines.plainText: Why this was moulded on a porringer

lines.text: A velvet dish: fie, fie! 'tis lewd and filthy:
lines.plainText: A velvet dish fie fie 'tis lewd and filthy

lines.text: Why, 'tis a cockle or a walnut-shell,
lines.plainText: Why 'tis a cockle or a walnutshell

lines.text: A knack, a toy, a trick, a baby's cap:
lines.plainText: A knack a toy a trick a baby's cap

lines.text: Away with it! come, let me have a bigger.
lines.plainText: Away with it come let me have a bigger

lines.text: I'll have no bigger; this doth fit the time,
lines.plainText: I'll have no bigger this doth fit the time

lines.text: And gentlewomen wear such caps as these.
lines.plainText: And gentlewomen wear such caps as these

lines.text: When you are gentle, you shall have one too,
lines.plainText: When you are gentle you shall have one too

lines.text: And not till then.
lines.plainText: And not till then

lines.text: [Aside] That will not be in haste.
lines.plainText: Aside That will not be in haste

lines.text: Why, sir, I trust I may have leave to speak;
lines.plainText: Why sir I trust I may have leave to speak

lines.text: And speak I will. I am no child, no babe.
lines.plainText: And speak I will I am no child no babe

lines.text: Your betters have endur'd me say my mind,
lines.plainText: Your betters have endur'd me say my mind

lines.text: And if you cannot, best you stop your ears.
lines.plainText: And if you cannot best you stop your ears

lines.text: My tongue will tell the anger of my heart,
lines.plainText: My tongue will tell the anger of my heart

lines.text: Or else my heart, concealing it, will break;
lines.plainText: Or else my heart concealing it will break

lines.text: And rather than it shall, I will be free
lines.plainText: And rather than it shall I will be free

lines.text: Even to the uttermost, as I please, in words.
lines.plainText: Even to the uttermost as I please in words

lines.text: Why, thou say'st true; it is a paltry cap,
lines.plainText: Why thou say'st true it is a paltry cap

lines.text: A custard-coffin, a bauble, a silken pie;
lines.plainText: A custardcoffin a bauble a silken pie

lines.text: I love thee well in that thou lik'st it not.
lines.plainText: I love thee well in that thou lik'st it not

lines.text: Love me or love me not, I like the cap;
lines.plainText: Love me or love me not I like the cap

lines.text: And it I will have, or I will have none.
lines.plainText: And it I will have or I will have none

lines.text: Thy gown? Why, ay: come, tailor, let us see't.
lines.plainText: Thy gown Why ay come tailor let us see't

lines.text: O mercy, God! what masquing stuff is here?
lines.plainText: O mercy God what masquing stuff is here

lines.text: What's this? A sleeve? 'Tis like a demi-cannon.
lines.plainText: What's this A sleeve 'Tis like a demicannon

lines.text: What, up and down, carv'd like an apple tart?
lines.plainText: What up and down carv'd like an apple tart

lines.text: Here's snip and nip and cut and slish and slash,
lines.plainText: Here's snip and nip and cut and slish and slash

lines.text: Like to a censer in a barber's shop.
lines.plainText: Like to a censer in a barber's shop

lines.text: Why, what i' devil's name, tailor, call'st thou this?
lines.plainText: Why what i' devil's name tailor call'st thou this

lines.text: [Aside] I see she's like to have neither cap nor gown.
lines.plainText: Aside I see she's like to have neither cap nor gown

lines.text: You bid me make it orderly and well,
lines.plainText: You bid me make it orderly and well

lines.text: According to the fashion and the time.
lines.plainText: According to the fashion and the time

lines.text: Marry, and did; but if you be remember'd,
lines.plainText: Marry and did but if you be remember'd

lines.text: I did not bid you mar it to the time.
lines.plainText: I did not bid you mar it to the time

lines.text: Go, hop me over every kennel home,
lines.plainText: Go hop me over every kennel home

lines.text: For you shall hop without my custom, sir.
lines.plainText: For you shall hop without my custom sir

lines.text: I'll none of it: hence! make your best of it.
lines.plainText: I'll none of it hence make your best of it

lines.text: I never saw a better fashion'd gown,
lines.plainText: I never saw a better fashion'd gown

lines.text: More quaint, more pleasing, nor more commendable;
lines.plainText: More quaint more pleasing nor more commendable

lines.text: Belike you mean to make a puppet of me.
lines.plainText: Belike you mean to make a puppet of me

lines.text: Why, true; he means to make a puppet of thee.
lines.plainText: Why true he means to make a puppet of thee

lines.text: She says your worship means to make a puppet of her.
lines.plainText: She says your worship means to make a puppet of her

lines.text: O monstrous arrogance! Thou liest, thou thread,
lines.plainText: O monstrous arrogance Thou liest thou thread

lines.text: Thou thimble,
lines.plainText: Thou thimble

lines.text: Thou yard, three-quarters, half-yard, quarter, nail!
lines.plainText: Thou yard threequarters halfyard quarter nail

lines.text: Thou flea, thou nit, thou winter-cricket thou!
lines.plainText: Thou flea thou nit thou wintercricket thou

lines.text: Brav'd in mine own house with a skein of thread!
lines.plainText: Brav'd in mine own house with a skein of thread

lines.text: Away! thou rag, thou quantity, thou remnant,
lines.plainText: Away thou rag thou quantity thou remnant

lines.text: Or I shall so be-mete thee with thy yard
lines.plainText: Or I shall so bemete thee with thy yard

lines.text: As thou shalt think on prating whilst thou liv'st!
lines.plainText: As thou shalt think on prating whilst thou liv'st

lines.text: I tell thee, I, that thou hast marr'd her gown.
lines.plainText: I tell thee I that thou hast marr'd her gown

lines.text: Your worship is deceiv'd: the gown is made
lines.plainText: Your worship is deceiv'd the gown is made

lines.text: Just as my master had direction.
lines.plainText: Just as my master had direction

lines.text: Grumio gave order how it should be done.
lines.plainText: Grumio gave order how it should be done

lines.text: I gave him no order; I gave him the stuff.
lines.plainText: I gave him no order I gave him the stuff

lines.text: But how did you desire it should be made?
lines.plainText: But how did you desire it should be made

lines.text: Marry, sir, with needle and thread.
lines.plainText: Marry sir with needle and thread

lines.text: But did you not request to have it cut?
lines.plainText: But did you not request to have it cut

lines.text: Thou hast faced many things.
lines.plainText: Thou hast faced many things

lines.text: I have.
lines.plainText: I have

lines.text: Face not me. Thou hast braved many men; brave not me: I will neither be fac'd nor brav'd. I say unto thee, I bid thy master cut out the gown; but I did not bid him cut it to pieces: ergo, thou liest.
lines.plainText: Face not me Thou hast braved many men brave not me I will neither be fac'd nor brav'd I say unto thee I bid thy master cut out the gown but I did not bid him cut it to pieces ergo thou liest

lines.text: Why, here is the note of the fashion to testify.
lines.plainText: Why here is the note of the fashion to testify

lines.text: Read it.
lines.plainText: Read it

lines.text: The note lies in 's throat, if he say I said so.
lines.plainText: The note lies in 's throat if he say I said so

lines.text: 'Imprimis, a loose-bodied gown.'
lines.plainText: 'Imprimis a loosebodied gown'

lines.text: Master, if ever I said loose-bodied gown, sew me in the skirts of it and beat me to death with a bottom of brown thread; I said, a gown.
lines.plainText: Master if ever I said loosebodied gown sew me in the skirts of it and beat me to death with a bottom of brown thread I said a gown

lines.text: Proceed.
lines.plainText: Proceed

lines.text: 'With a small compassed cape.'
lines.plainText: 'With a small compassed cape'

lines.text: I confess the cape.
lines.plainText: I confess the cape

lines.text: 'With a trunk sleeve.'
lines.plainText: 'With a trunk sleeve'

lines.text: I confess two sleeves.
lines.plainText: I confess two sleeves

lines.text: 'The sleeves curiously cut.'
lines.plainText: 'The sleeves curiously cut'

lines.text: Ay, there's the villainy.
lines.plainText: Ay there's the villainy

lines.text: Error i' the bill, sir; error i' the bill. I commanded the sleeves should be cut out, and sew'd up again; and that I'll prove upon thee, though thy little finger be armed in a thimble.
lines.plainText: Error i' the bill sir error i' the bill I commanded the sleeves should be cut out and sew'd up again and that I'll prove upon thee though thy little finger be armed in a thimble

lines.text: This is true that I say; and I had thee in place where thou shouldst know it.
lines.plainText: This is true that I say and I had thee in place where thou shouldst know it

lines.text: I am for thee straight; take thou the bill, give me thy mete-yard, and spare not me.
lines.plainText: I am for thee straight take thou the bill give me thy meteyard and spare not me

lines.text: God-a-mercy, Grumio! Then he shall have no odds.
lines.plainText: Godamercy Grumio Then he shall have no odds

lines.text: Well, sir, in brief, the gown is not for me.
lines.plainText: Well sir in brief the gown is not for me

lines.text: You are i' the right, sir; 'tis for my mistress.
lines.plainText: You are i' the right sir 'tis for my mistress

lines.text: Go, take it up unto thy master's use.
lines.plainText: Go take it up unto thy master's use

lines.text: Villain, not for thy life! Take up my mistress' gown for thy master's use!
lines.plainText: Villain not for thy life Take up my mistress' gown for thy master's use

lines.text: Why, sir, what's your conceit in that?
lines.plainText: Why sir what's your conceit in that

lines.text: O, sir, the conceit is deeper than you think for.
lines.plainText: O sir the conceit is deeper than you think for

lines.text: Take up my mistress' gown to his master's use!
lines.plainText: Take up my mistress' gown to his master's use

lines.text: O fie, fie, fie!
lines.plainText: O fie fie fie

lines.text: [Aside] Hortensio, say thou wilt see the tailor paid.
lines.plainText: Aside Hortensio say thou wilt see the tailor paid

lines.text: [To Tailor.] Go take it hence; be gone, and say no more.
lines.plainText: To Tailor Go take it hence be gone and say no more

lines.text: [Aside to Tailor.] Tailor, I'll pay thee for thy gown tomorrow;
lines.plainText: Aside to Tailor Tailor I'll pay thee for thy gown tomorrow

lines.text: Take no unkindness of his hasty words.
lines.plainText: Take no unkindness of his hasty words

lines.text: Away, I say! commend me to thy master.
lines.plainText: Away I say commend me to thy master

lines.text: Well, come, my Kate; we will unto your father's
lines.plainText: Well come my Kate we will unto your father's

lines.text: Even in these honest mean habiliments.
lines.plainText: Even in these honest mean habiliments

lines.text: Our purses shall be proud, our garments poor
lines.plainText: Our purses shall be proud our garments poor

lines.text: For 'tis the mind that makes the body rich;
lines.plainText: For 'tis the mind that makes the body rich

lines.text: And as the sun breaks through the darkest clouds,
lines.plainText: And as the sun breaks through the darkest clouds

lines.text: So honour peereth in the meanest habit.
lines.plainText: So honour peereth in the meanest habit

lines.text: What, is the jay more precious than the lark
lines.plainText: What is the jay more precious than the lark

lines.text: Because his feathers are more beautiful?
lines.plainText: Because his feathers are more beautiful

lines.text: Or is the adder better than the eel
lines.plainText: Or is the adder better than the eel

lines.text: Because his painted skin contents the eye?
lines.plainText: Because his painted skin contents the eye

lines.text: O no, good Kate; neither art thou the worse
lines.plainText: O no good Kate neither art thou the worse

lines.text: For this poor furniture and mean array.
lines.plainText: For this poor furniture and mean array

lines.text: If thou account'st it shame, lay it on me;
lines.plainText: If thou account'st it shame lay it on me

lines.text: And therefore frolic; we will hence forthwith,
lines.plainText: And therefore frolic we will hence forthwith

lines.text: To feast and sport us at thy father's house.
lines.plainText: To feast and sport us at thy father's house

lines.text: Go call my men, and let us straight to him;
lines.plainText: Go call my men and let us straight to him

lines.text: And bring our horses unto Long-lane end;
lines.plainText: And bring our horses unto Longlane end

lines.text: There will we mount, and thither walk on foot.
lines.plainText: There will we mount and thither walk on foot

lines.text: Let's see; I think 'tis now some seven o'clock,
lines.plainText: Let's see I think 'tis now some seven o'clock

lines.text: And well we may come there by dinner-time.
lines.plainText: And well we may come there by dinnertime

lines.text: I dare assure you, sir, 'tis almost two,
lines.plainText: I dare assure you sir 'tis almost two

lines.text: And 'twill be supper-time ere you come there.
lines.plainText: And 'twill be suppertime ere you come there

lines.text: It shall be seven ere I go to horse.
lines.plainText: It shall be seven ere I go to horse

lines.text: Look what I speak, or do, or think to do,
lines.plainText: Look what I speak or do or think to do

lines.text: You are still crossing it. Sirs, let 't alone:
lines.plainText: You are still crossing it Sirs let 't alone

lines.text: I will not go today; and ere I do,
lines.plainText: I will not go today and ere I do

lines.text: It shall be what o'clock I say it is.
lines.plainText: It shall be what o'clock I say it is

lines.text: Why, so this gallant will command the sun.
lines.plainText: Why so this gallant will command the sun
